newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on crop condition ratings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on crop condition ratings.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on the bearish tone linked to USDA's weekly crop condition ratings, traders said.
USDA Monday said as of Sunday, the U.S. winter wheat crop rated 53 percent good to excellent, above the 50 percent in that category the previous week.
Traders also said the market was pressed by the sharp drop in prices Monday which stemmed from Monday's USDA May crop production and supply/demand reports.
USDA Monday pegged 1997 U.S. winter wheat production at 1.561 billion bushels, six percent above last year's outturn.

Freezing temperatures in the U.S. Great Plains in mid-April damaged some of the hard red winter wheat crop, USDA reported, but the yield losses were not as severe as some had expected. USDA forecast U.S. HRW wheat production this year would total 893.9 million bushels, sharply above last year's 762.4 million bushel output.
But wheat held key support and ended the day above the day's lows.
Wheat closed one to five cents per bushel lower, with May down five at $3.88 a bushel. July was 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower at $3.95-1/2.
